description: packages/storage/src/config/storage.ts exposes a user-upload validator that keeps the current allowlist plus size behavior, extracted from validateFileUpload with no behavior change.
packages/storage/src/config/storage.ts exposes a system-artifact validator that enforces provider size limits and skips the MIME allowlist entirely.
StorageService.uploadStream accepts a named provenance option ('user-upload' | 'system-artifact') that selects the validator; omitting it yields user-upload behavior.
StorageService.uploadFile accepts the same provenance option with the same default, leaving its image-processing branches untouched.
/api/migrations/spreadsheet stores the converted AMP package as a system artifact.
/api/migrations/upload stores the uploaded AMP package as a system artifact.
/api/migrations/upload stores a fixed AMP MIME type instead of echoing the request content-type header.
invoiceZipHandler stores the generated invoice bundle as a system artifact.
documentPreviewGenerator stores thumbnail and preview renditions as system artifacts, in both the server and packages copies.
telephonyCallArtifactHandler and onlineMeetingArtifactActions store fetched provider artifacts as system artifacts.
A closed set of migration upload error codes is defined in one module shared by the routes and the UI.
/api/migrations/spreadsheet returns only codes from that set; an unrecognized throw becomes a generic failure code.
/api/migrations/upload returns only codes from that set, with the same generic fallback.
A storage-layer rejection maps to a distinct code separating deployment misconfiguration from a bad file.
Unrecognized throws are logged server-side with tenant and route context before the generic code is returned.
migrationUi exposes a code-to-copy mapping with i18n keys and default values covering every emitted code, plus a fallback for unknown codes.
UploadPackageDialog renders mapped copy through that helper, replacing the single inline special case and the raw message pass-through.
Locale strings for every migration upload error code are added to the msp/settings namespace.
inferSpreadsheetMapping resolves aliases from an entity-scoped table rather than one shared map, preserving current asset behavior.
Alias lookup normalizes separators consistently, so a header matches whether it is spaced, underscored, or hyphenated.
Contacts aliases cover the common spellings for email, first name, last name, phone, and title.
Organizations aliases cover client, company, and account name spellings.
The conversion engine supports a derived-column transform, so one source header can populate more than one target column.
A single full-name contacts column splits into first and last name, handling both 'First Last' and 'Last, First'.
Contacts carry a required-column set, so a row with no name or no email is skipped at conversion with a diagnostic instead of throwing at apply.
A client or company column on a contacts sheet is carried through conversion instead of being discarded into extension_json.
The contacts applier resolves a carried client name against existing tenant clients, falling back to the configured default client.
An unmatched client name produces a diagnostic rather than rejecting the row or the job.
Conversion emits a diagnostic naming every header that did not map to a column.
The upload dialog surfaces conversion diagnostics on a successful stage, so ignored columns are visible before apply.
The hosted attachment allowlist is reviewed against product behavior and the finding is recorded in the scratchpad with a recommendation and the exact values-file locations.

A spreadsheet import derives its identity namespace from the SHA-256 of the uploaded source bytes, so two different sheets never share an identity key while re-uploading identical bytes stays idempotent.
The migration report service exposes skip provenance: the prior jobs whose identity mappings claimed this job's skipped records, with their package digest and source file name.

The results panel makes the 'same package' skip claim only when the claiming mappings came from this package; otherwise it names the prior migration or says the rows matched existing entities, and labels each skipped record's origin.
A completed job that created nothing but skipped rows is surfaced as a warning badge and a warning panel instead of a plain green Completed.
